newsitem.title: USA: Genzyme Tissue shrs dip, analysts hopeful.
newsitem.headline: Genzyme Tissue shrs dip, analysts hopeful.

text.p: Genzyme Corp's Tissue Repair division shares slipped on Friday after a U.S. Food and Drug Administration panel said more long-term study was needed to understand why its treatment for knee cartilage repair worked.

In an 11 to zero vote, the FDA's Orthopedic and Rehabilitation Devices panel said on Thursday the Carticel treatment, which involved harvesting cartilage cells and reinserting them into the knee area, seemed to help patients but called for more study on why.
But analysts said it was normal for the FDA to require more data for the treatment because it never went through the rite of FDA standardized clinical trials.
Carticel, out since 1995 and one of Genzyme Tissue's two products on the market, was reviewed by the government agency but never regulated because it fell outside existing policies.

"The company did studies on the product, but there were no Phase III, double-blinded, placebo-controlled studies per se," said Edmund Debler, an analyst at Mehta and Isaly. "It's normal that the FDA would want more data."
Genzyme Tissue said it has already planned a five-year clinical study, which compared Carticel to other treatment options available to repair damaged knee cartilage.

Cowen and Co analyst David Stone said in a research note that based on the review, he expected full FDA approval of Carticel in the first half of 1997, easing reimbursement and boosting sales of the product.
He projected sales growth from $3 million in 1996 to $12 million in 1997 and $60 million in 1998.
But other analysts were more cautious, uncertain how long it would take Genzyme to generate the required data.

"It's disappointing," one analyst said. "The FDA has allowed the company to keep marketing the procedure, but it was more the quality and quantity of the data. The FDA didn't seem to feel it had the data in front of them."
Shares closed off 7/8 at 12-1/4, above an intraday low of 11-1/8, after being halted on Nasdaq Thursday, while the panel met.

Anne Anderson, an analyst at Atlantis Research, said on Thursday: "If it (the panel review) doesn't go well, it won't prevent doctors already using the techology, but Genzyme Tissue needs FDA approval in order to grow the market."
